name: CRISPR Systems Enable Efficient Genome Editing Across Diverse Organisms
anchorClaim: CRISPR-based nuclease systems (Cas9 and related tools such as TALENs and TnpB) enable efficient, reproducible genome editing across bacterial, fungal, and parasitic organisms, with documented editing efficiency and off-target rates reported in the primary literature.
plainQuestion: Does CRISPR-based genome editing (Cas9 and related tools like TALENs and TnpB) work efficiently and reproducibly across many different organisms, not just one well-studied species?

guide.whatScienceSays: Across the 233 real datoms collected for this claim, 216 (92.7%) support efficient CRISPR-based genome editing across bacterial, fungal, and parasitic systems, 15 (6.4%) are conditional or mixed, and 2 (0.9%) explicitly contradict the general efficiency claim. The evidence spans bacteria (E. coli, other bacterial strains), fungi (including protoplast and multiplex editing systems), and parasitic and mammalian systems, using tools including Cas9, Cas12a, TALENs, and TnpB, with editing efficiency and off-target detection methods (e.g. GUIDE-seq, CIRCLE-seq, T7EI assays) reported in individual studies.
guide.howConfident: The confidence_band is Preliminary at a 35/100 score despite 233 replications because the underlying evidence base is directionally consistent but methodologically thin: sample size was not reported for 111 of the 233 datoms (about half), and methodology descriptions are almost entirely unique free text (208 distinct methodology strings across 233 datoms), which limits the ability to synthesize a single quantitative effect size or standardize across studies. Evidence completeness is also split, with 103 of 233 datoms extracted as text without full metadata versus 130 with full-text PDF access.
decisionSupport: CRISPR/Cas9 and related nucleases (TALENs, TnpB) show consistent directional support for genome editing efficiency across bacterial, fungal, and parasitic systems in the literature reviewed (216 of 233 datoms, 92.7%).

Off-target rate reporting is inconsistent across studies; check whether an off-target assay (e.g. GUIDE-seq, CIRCLE-seq) was actually performed for your specific organism or system rather than assuming results generalize.
Sample size was not reported in about half of the underlying records (111 of 233), so treat pooled efficiency figures as directional rather than statistically precise.
Two datoms explicitly contradict the general efficiency claim; review those specific cases before treating the claim as universal across all target organisms.
guide.faultLines: Nearly half the underlying records (111 of 233) do not report a sample size, and methodology descriptions are essentially unique per study (208 distinct methodology strings across 233 datoms), which limits cross-study standardization and any pooled quantitative synthesis. Evidence completeness is also uneven, with 103 of 233 datoms extracted as text without full source metadata.

dataQualityNote: Correct data linkage required using projectId (bd50104d-463a-4577-a7f0-09a2f1c8a6d0) rather than the datomerId GSI as originally specified: individual datom records carry an unrelated batch-level datomerId field, and querying that GSI with the Datomer's own id returned zero results. The projectId query returned exactly 233 items whose datom_id set exactly matches the Datomer's own datom_ids list and its replication_count, confirming this is the true complete dataset. One of 233 datoms is missing source_year. Methodology descriptions are highly granular free text (208 distinct values across 233 datoms, most appearing only once), so methodologyMix contains many singleton categories rather than a small number of clean buckets; no categories were merged or invented. Sample size was not reported for 111 of 233 datoms.

datoms.claim: CRISPR-Cas9 system enables efficient genome editing in Escherichia coli, achieving up to 100% editing efficiency for gene deletion and insertion.
datoms.source: Yu Jiang, Biao Chen, Chunlan Duan, Bingbing Sun, Junjie Yang. "Multigene Editing in the Escherichia coli Genome via the CRISPR-Cas9 System" (2015). doi:10.1128/aem.04023-14
datoms.measure: Genome editing efficiency for gene deletion and insertion
datoms.methodology: Targeted multigene editing in bacterial genome

datoms.claim: CRISPR/Cas9 system enables efficient gene disruption in the fungal organism Lipomyces starkeyi, as demonstrated by frameshift mutations and loss of GFP fluorescence.
datoms.source: Rikako Sato, Kaito Maruyama, Satoshi Ara, Masayuki Shibata, Yosuke Shida. "A CRISPR/Cas9-based genome-editing platform enabling efficient and precise gene replacement in Lipomyces starkeyi." (2026). doi:10.1093/femsyr/foag014
datoms.population: Lipomyces starkeyi CBS1807 wild-type and ∆lslig4 strains
datoms.measure: GFP fluorescence loss and frameshift mutations at target locus
datoms.methodology: In vivo GFP disruption assay with sequencing validation
datoms.sample_size: 10 colonies sequenced for sgRNA(GFP1); 10 colonies for sgRNA(GFP2)
datoms.notes: Study found possible off-target cleavage by sgRNA(GFP1) at sites near the target; no genome-wide off-target screen was performed.

datoms.claim: CRISPR-Cas9 ribonucleoprotein complexes enable precise targeted gene editing in maize, with documented editing efficiency for endogenous gene modification.
datoms.source: Sergei Svitashev, Christine Schwartz, Brian Lenderts, Joshua K. Young, A. Mark Cigan. "Genome editing in maize directed by CRISPR–Cas9 ribonucleoprotein complexes" (2016). doi:10.1038/ncomms13274
datoms.population: Maize (Zea mays) Hi-II immature embryo cells
datoms.measure: Precise targeted gene editing efficiency (homology-directed repair at ALS2 locus)
datoms.methodology: Biolistic delivery with homology-directed repair template and herbicide selection
datoms.sample_size: 40-50 bombarded embryos per experiment; 2 independent experiments
datoms.notes: Only two independent experiments were run for the ALS2 edit, and the paper does not report HDR frequency relative to total embryos bombarded.

datoms.claim: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated gene knockout achieves 90.8% mRNA reduction in MDA-MB-231 cancer cells, outperforming commercial Lipofectamine reagent (51.1% reduction).
datoms.source: Xinpu Yang, Rui Sang, Gyorgy Hutvagner, Alex W Hewitt, Diangeng Li. "An optimised lipid nanoparticle platform enables efficient CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing in hard-to-transfect cells." (2026). doi:10.1016/j.actbio.2026.05.044
datoms.measure: LCN2 gene knockout efficiency (mRNA reduction %)
datoms.methodology: In vitro cell transfection with lipid nanoparticles and comparative analysis
datoms.notes: Testing was limited to an in vitro cancer cell line, so generalizability to other cell types or in vivo systems is not established.

datoms.claim: CRISPR-Cas9 system enables precise deletion of multi-kilobase genomic regions in parasitic organisms, as demonstrated by successful 3-kb gene deletion in Leishmania donovani.
datoms.source: Wen‐Wei Zhang, Greg Matlashewski. "CRISPR-Cas9-Mediated Genome Editing in Leishmania donovani" (2015). doi:10.1128/mbio.00861-15
datoms.measure: Precise deletion efficiency of multi-kilobase genomic regions
datoms.methodology: Experimental genome editing with dual-gRNA vectors

datoms.claim: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated genome editing achieves high knockout efficiency in human cell lines, with GFP knockout reaching 78.7% in HEK-293 cells.
datoms.source: Xinpu Yang, Rui Sang, Gyorgy Hutvagner, Alex W Hewitt, Diangeng Li. "An optimised lipid nanoparticle platform enables efficient CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing in hard-to-transfect cells." (2026). doi:10.1016/j.actbio.2026.05.044
datoms.measure: GFP knockout efficiency (%)
datoms.methodology: In vitro cell transfection with lipid nanoparticles
datoms.notes: Testing was limited to in vitro cell lines; applicability to in vivo systems or other organisms was not addressed.

datoms.claim: CRISPR/Cas9 systems enable efficient genome editing in Penicillium chrysogenum, a filamentous fungus.
datoms.source: Craig Pohl, Jan A.K.W. Kiel, Arnold J. M. Driessen, Roel A. L. Bovenberg, Yvonne Nygård. "CRISPR/Cas9 Based Genome Editing of Penicillium chrysogenum" (2016). doi:10.1021/acssynbio.6b00082
datoms.measure: Efficiency of marker-based and marker-free genome modifications
datoms.methodology: In vitro genome editing with CRISPR/Cas9 ribonucleoproteins and plasmid expression

datoms.claim: CRISPR/Cas9 system enables simultaneous targeting and editing of multiple genes in filamentous fungi.
datoms.source: Rui Liu, Ling Chen, Yanping Jiang, Zhihua Zhou, Gen Zou. "Efficient genome editing in filamentous fungus Trichoderma reesei using the CRISPR/Cas9 system" (2015). doi:10.1038/celldisc.2015.7
datoms.measure: Capability for simultaneous multi-gene targeting
datoms.methodology: Experimental multiplexed genome editing in fungal cells
datoms.notes: The paper does not report quantitative multiplexing efficiency or success rates.

datoms.claim: Ex vivo CRISPR editing in hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) using clinically relevant workflows produces fewer than one true off-target site per guide RNA on average.
datoms.source: Beeke Wienert, M. Kyle Cromer. "CRISPR nuclease off-target activity and mitigation strategies" (2022). doi:10.3389/fgeed.2022.1050507
datoms.population: Hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) in clinically relevant workflows
datoms.domain: Genome editing efficiency and off-target activity
datoms.measure: Frequency of bonafide off-target sites per guide RNA
datoms.methodology: Ex vivo HSPC editing with comprehensive off-target detection
datoms.notes: Testing was limited to HSPCs in an ex vivo setting, so results may not generalize to other cell types or in vivo use.

datoms.claim: CRISPR-Cas9 enables efficient genome editing in Saccharomyces cerevisiae (yeast) through Cas9-targeted DNA breaks that promote homologous recombination with mutagenic template DNA.
datoms.source: Marian F. Laughery, John J. Wyrick. "Simple CRISPR‐Cas9 Genome Editing in Saccharomyces cerevisiae" (2019). doi:10.1002/cpmb.110
datoms.measure: Efficiency of genome editing (DNA substitutions, insertions, deletions)
datoms.methodology: Protocol development and genome editing demonstration
datoms.notes: This is a protocol paper; it does not report quantitative editing efficiency or off-target rates.

datoms.claim: Cas9 nuclease systems demonstrate measurable off-target editing activity in mammalian cells, with specificity rates quantifiable through unbiased genome-wide assessment.
datoms.source: Vikram Pattanayak, John P. Guilinger, David R. Liu. "Determining the Specificities of TALENs, Cas9, and Other Genome-Editing Enzymes" (2014). doi:10.1016/b978-0-12-801185-0.00003-9
datoms.population: mammalian cells (HEK293T human embryonic kidney cells)
datoms.measure: off-target cleavage frequency and specificity rates
datoms.methodology: Unbiased genome-wide off-target assessment in mammalian cells
datoms.notes: Testing was done in mammalian cell lines and detects cleavage events without necessarily predicting their functional consequences.

datoms.claim: CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing has been successfully established in more than 40 different species of filamentous fungi and oomycetes.
datoms.source: Mariana Schuster, Regine Kahmann. "CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing approaches in filamentous fungi and oomycetes" (2019). doi:10.1016/j.fgb.2019.04.016
datoms.measure: Number of species in which CRISPR-Cas9 system has been established
datoms.methodology: Literature review and synthesis
datoms.notes: This is a review article; it synthesizes existing work rather than presenting original efficiency or off-target data.

datoms.claim: CRISPR-Cas9 system achieves single gene editing efficiency of 31.7% in Aspergillus niger when using a single guide RNA targeting the albA locus.
datoms.source: Guoliang Yuan, Shuang Deng, Jeffrey J. Czajka, Ziyu Dai, Beth A. Hofstad. "CRISPR-Cas9/Cas12a systems for efficient genome editing and large genomic fragment deletions in Aspergillus niger" (2024). doi:10.3389/fbioe.2024.1452496
datoms.measure: Genome editing efficiency (percentage of edited colonies)
datoms.methodology: Protoplast transformation with single colony isolation and PCR genotyping
datoms.notes: Three biological replicates were run for most vectors (fewer for pGY177 and pGY178), and single colonies were isolated 19 to 24 hours post-transformation, before colonies were visible to the naked eye.

datoms.claim: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated editing of StDND2 in potato results in a consistent T→G nucleotide substitution (missense mutation: leucine-to-glutamine) that is maintained across T0 and T1 generations.
datoms.source: Arsh Bibi, Irshad Ullah, Shaheen Aftab, Imran Amin, Bushra Bibi. "Genome editing of susceptibility gene StDND2 enhances Phytophthora resistance in Solanum tuberosum." (2026). doi:10.3389/fpls.2026.1807632
datoms.population: Solanum tuberosum cv. Kuroda T0 and T1 transgenic lines
datoms.domain: CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing efficiency and mutation characterization
datoms.measure: Nucleotide substitution type and consistency across generations and allelic copies
datoms.methodology: Targeted next-generation sequencing (NGS) of genomic DNA
datoms.sample_size: Multiple edited T0 plants and corresponding T1 progeny
datoms.notes: Whether editing events across the analyzed lines were truly independent could not be conclusively determined, and analysis was limited to the T0 and T1 generations.

datoms.claim: CRISPR/Cas9 system enables efficient genome editing in the filamentous fungus Trichoderma reesei through site-specific mutations via homologous recombination.
datoms.source: Rui Liu, Ling Chen, Yanping Jiang, Zhihua Zhou, Gen Zou. "Efficient genome editing in filamentous fungus Trichoderma reesei using the CRISPR/Cas9 system" (2015). doi:10.1038/celldisc.2015.7
datoms.measure: Site-specific mutation efficiency and homologous recombination capability
datoms.methodology: Experimental genome editing with codon optimization and inducible expression
datoms.notes: The paper does not report quantitative editing efficiency percentages or off-target mutation rates.

datoms.claim: CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing produces substantially fewer off-target effects compared to existing genome editing methods.
datoms.source: Ophir Shalem, Neville E. Sanjana, E. Hartenian, Xi Shi, David A. Scott. "Genome-Scale CRISPR-Cas9 Knockout Screening in Human Cells" (2014). doi:10.1126/science.1247005
datoms.population: Human cells (cancer and pluripotent stem cells)
datoms.measure: Off-target effects rate relative to siRNA and existing methods
datoms.methodology: Comparative analysis of CRISPR-Cas9 versus siRNA and other genome editing methods
datoms.notes: Off-target rates are described qualitatively rather than with specific numbers.

datoms.claim: Double-nicking strategy using Cas9 nickase mutant with paired guide RNAs reduces off-target cleavage in mammalian cells.
datoms.source: F. Ran, P. Hsu, Jason B Wright, Vineeta Agarwala, Vineeta Agarwala. "Genome engineering using the CRISPR-Cas9 system" (2013). doi:10.1038/nprot.2013.143
datoms.measure: off-target cleavage activity
datoms.methodology: Experimental protocol development
datoms.notes: This protocol paper proposes the double-nicking strategy without extensive quantitative off-target validation.

datoms.claim: CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing induces large structural variants (>50 Kb) at off-target sites without sequence similarity to the sgRNA in edited human pluripotent stem cells.
datoms.source: Hsiu-Hui Tsai, H. Kao, Ming-Wei Kuo, Chin-Hsien Lin, Chunghun Chang. "Whole genomic analysis reveals atypical non-homologous off-target large structural variants induced by CRISPR-Cas9-mediated genome editing" (2023). doi:10.1038/s41467-023-40901-x
datoms.population: Human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs), 13 edited cell lines
datoms.measure: Off-target large structural variants (deletions) at non-homologous sites without sgRNA sequence similarity
datoms.methodology: Linked-read sequencing, optical genome mapping, PCR validation
datoms.notes: Of 13 iPSC lines examined, only 2 showed the atypical off-target structural variants, and the underlying mechanism remains unclear; delivery was by plasmid DNA, so RNP delivery effects were not directly tested.

datoms.claim: CRISPR/Cas9 with 5′-truncated sgRNAs enables efficient single-base genome editing in bacterial cells (E. coli), with editing efficiency reaching 80-83% for galK targets and 63% overall success rate across multiple target positions.
datoms.source: Ho Joung Lee, H. Kim, S. J. Lee. "Mismatch Intolerance of 5′-Truncated sgRNAs in CRISPR/Cas9 Enables Efficient Microbial Single-Base Genome Editing" (2021). doi:10.3390/ijms22126457
datoms.population: E. coli MG1655 cells with chromosomally integrated cas9 gene
datoms.measure: Single-base editing efficiency (percentage of white colonies indicating successful single-base mutations)
datoms.methodology: Bacterial colony selection and Sanger sequencing
datoms.sample_size: 4 randomly selected colonies per electroporation; 3 independent experiments
datoms.notes: Editing failed at bases 10 nucleotides from the PAM in some targets (T508, T648) even though it succeeded there in other genes, and standard Cas9's 5'-NGG PAM requirement restricts targeting range.

datoms.claim: CRISPR/Cas9-based genome editing in Stropharia rugosoannulata shows no detectable off-target effects at predicted off-target sites.
datoms.source: Haibo Hao, Shuzhen Song, Qian Wang, Zongjun Tong, Wen Xu. "Unlocking the Potential for Genetic Engineering of the Straw-Degrading Mushroom Stropharia rugosoannulata by Constructing a CRISPR/Cas9 Gene Editing System." (2026). doi:10.3390/jof12040269
datoms.population: Stropharia rugosoannulata edited strains (T26, T32, T101, T127)
datoms.measure: Off-target editing events detected at predicted off-target sites
datoms.methodology: Whole-genome off-target prediction with deep sequencing validation
datoms.notes: Only 8 of 20 predicted off-target sites were experimentally tested, detection was limited to sites with 3 to 4 mismatches, and no quantitative off-target rate is reported.

datoms.claim: CRISPR/Cas9 system enables efficient genome editing in amphioxus (a non-mammalian chordate organism) with documented mutation efficiency rates.
datoms.source: Liuru Su, Chenggang Shi, Xin Huang, Yiquan Wang, Guang Li. "Application of CRISPR/Cas9 Nuclease in Amphioxus Genome Editing" (2020). doi:10.3390/genes11111311
datoms.population: Amphioxus (Branchiostoma floridae) unfertilized eggs and embryos
datoms.measure: Mutation efficiency (percentage of target sites mutagenized)
datoms.methodology: Microinjection of Cas9 protein and sgRNA into amphioxus embryos with T7EI cleavage assay and DNA sequencing
datoms.sample_size: 100-200 unfertilized eggs or 50 two-cell embryos per experiment
datoms.notes: Testing covered only nine sgRNAs across five genes in a single amphioxus species, and off-target effects were not systematically evaluated.

datoms.claim: CRISPR/Cas9 system in L. starkeyi exhibits occasional off-target cleavage at proximal genomic sites with partial sgRNA complementarity, similar to observations in S. cerevisiae.
datoms.source: Rikako Sato, Kaito Maruyama, Satoshi Ara, Masayuki Shibata, Yosuke Shida. "A CRISPR/Cas9-based genome-editing platform enabling efficient and precise gene replacement in Lipomyces starkeyi." (2026). doi:10.1093/femsyr/foag014
datoms.measure: Off-target cleavage frequency at proximal sites
datoms.methodology: DNA sequencing of mutant loci following CRISPR/Cas9 treatment
datoms.notes: Off-target analysis was not genome-wide; it covered only the AcGFP locus and only one of the two sgRNAs tested.

datoms.claim: CRISPR-Cas12a system achieves large genomic fragment deletion efficiency of up to 60.4% in Aspergillus niger, with deletions ranging from 20.8 kb to 101.8 kb.
datoms.source: Guoliang Yuan, Shuang Deng, Jeffrey J. Czajka, Ziyu Dai, Beth A. Hofstad. "CRISPR-Cas9/Cas12a systems for efficient genome editing and large genomic fragment deletions in Aspergillus niger" (2024). doi:10.3389/fbioe.2024.1452496
datoms.measure: Large genomic fragment deletion efficiency (percentage of edited colonies)
datoms.methodology: Protoplast transformation with multi-gRNA targeting and PCR genotyping validation
datoms.notes: Data on the pGY158 and pGY176 constructs were insufficient because isolated colonies failed to grow, possibly due to disruption of essential genes.

datoms.claim: CRISPR-Cas9 system achieves large genomic fragment deletion efficiency of up to 69.1% in Aspergillus niger, with deletions ranging from 3.5 kb to 40.5 kb.
datoms.source: Guoliang Yuan, Shuang Deng, Jeffrey J. Czajka, Ziyu Dai, Beth A. Hofstad. "CRISPR-Cas9/Cas12a systems for efficient genome editing and large genomic fragment deletions in Aspergillus niger" (2024). doi:10.3389/fbioe.2024.1452496
datoms.measure: Large genomic fragment deletion efficiency (percentage of edited colonies)
datoms.methodology: Protoplast transformation with multi-gRNA targeting and PCR genotyping validation
datoms.sample_size: 3 biological replicates for pGY42, pGY56, pGY76, pGY77, pGY108, pGY175
datoms.notes: Data on the pGY109, pGY158, and pGY176 constructs were insufficient because isolated colonies failed to grow, possibly due to disruption of essential genes.

datoms.claim: CRISPR-Cas9 ribonucleoprotein complexes enable efficient genome editing in maize, with documented editing efficiency measured by mutation frequency at target sites.
datoms.source: Sergei Svitashev, Christine Schwartz, Brian Lenderts, Joshua K. Young, A. Mark Cigan. "Genome editing in maize directed by CRISPR–Cas9 ribonucleoprotein complexes" (2016). doi:10.1038/ncomms13274
datoms.population: Maize (Zea mays) Hi-II immature embryo cells
datoms.measure: Mutation frequency at target sites (NHEJ mutations detected by deep sequencing)
datoms.methodology: Biolistic delivery with amplicon deep sequencing
datoms.sample_size: 30 embryos pooled for deep sequencing; 60 embryos for plant regeneration experiments
datoms.notes: Testing focused on maize and did not extensively cover other crops; off-target analysis covered only one site for MS45, and mutation stability beyond the T1 generation was not reported for most targets.

datoms.claim: CRISPR-Cas9 enables efficient genome editing in Leishmania parasites, including gene deletion, precise editing, and endogenous locus tagging.
datoms.source: Anıl Ata, Derya Topuz Ata. "A comprehensive review of CRISPR-Cas9-mediated genome editing in Leishmania strains: methodologies, applications, challenges and future directions." (2026). doi:10.1007/s11033-026-12285-w
datoms.measure: Genome editing efficiency across multiple editing modalities (gene deletion, precise editing, locus tagging)
datoms.methodology: Systematic literature review and synthesis
datoms.notes: This review identifies constraints such as genome plasticity, multicopy gene families, essential-gene targeting, guide design limits, and off-target considerations, without presenting new experimental data.

datoms.claim: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated precise genome editing achieves efficiency rates of up to 45% in induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) with co-delivered Cas9 RNP and donor DNA.
datoms.source: Xiquan Liang, J. Potter, Shantanu Kumar, N. Ravinder, J. Chesnut. "Enhanced CRISPR/Cas9-mediated precise genome editing by improved design and delivery of gRNA, Cas9 nuclease, and donor DNA." (2017). doi:10.1016/j.jbiotec.2016.11.011
datoms.measure: Precise genome editing efficiency (%)
datoms.methodology: Cell-based genome editing with RNP delivery
datoms.notes: Testing was limited to mammalian cell systems; applicability to bacterial, fungal, or parasitic organisms was not evaluated.

datoms.claim: CRISPR-Cas9 systems enable genome editing with measurable off-target rates that have been documented and characterized in the primary literature.
datoms.source: Daisy Li, Hong Zhou, Xiao Zeng. "Battling CRISPR-Cas9 off-target genome editing" (2019). doi:10.1007/s10565-019-09485-5
datoms.population: CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing studies across multiple organisms
datoms.measure: Off-target editing rates and characterization
datoms.methodology: Literature review and analysis
datoms.notes: This review article synthesizes existing literature rather than reporting original quantitative off-target data.

datoms.claim: CRISPR-Cas9 enables gene disruptions, gene replacements, and precise editing in filamentous fungi and oomycetes through varying strategies.
datoms.source: Mariana Schuster, Regine Kahmann. "CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing approaches in filamentous fungi and oomycetes" (2019). doi:10.1016/j.fgb.2019.04.016
datoms.measure: Types of genome editing outcomes achieved (disruptions, replacements, precise edits)
datoms.methodology: Literature review and synthesis
datoms.notes: This review does not provide quantitative efficiency or off-target data and presents no original experimental validation.

datoms.claim: Cas9 nucleases produce indels (1-2 bp) or larger deletions (20-30 bp) that include loss of the PAM site, whereas LbCas12a produces deletions (2-20 bp) without PAM site loss.
datoms.source: R. Banakar, Mollie S. Schubert, Michael A. Collingwood, Christopher A. Vakulskas, A. Eggenberger. "Comparison of CRISPR-Cas9/Cas12a Ribonucleoprotein Complexes for Genome Editing Efficiency in the Rice Phytoene Desaturase (OsPDS) Gene" (2020). doi:10.1186/s12284-019-0365-z
datoms.population: Rice (Oryza sativa) callus lines derived from embryos
datoms.measure: Type and size of mutations (indels, deletions) and PAM site preservation
datoms.methodology: NGS analysis of edited rice callus lines
datoms.sample_size: 15 edited lines analyzed (2 WT Cas9, 3 HiFi Cas9, 10 LbCas12a)
datoms.notes: Analysis was done on callus tissue, which can be mosaic for mutations; sample size was limited and only one target site was evaluated.

datoms.claim: CRISPR/Cas9 system achieves genome editing in the fungal organism Stropharia rugosoannulata with documented editing efficiency of 14.9% at the ura3 locus.
datoms.source: Haibo Hao, Shuzhen Song, Qian Wang, Zongjun Tong, Wen Xu. "Unlocking the Potential for Genetic Engineering of the Straw-Degrading Mushroom Stropharia rugosoannulata by Constructing a CRISPR/Cas9 Gene Editing System." (2026). doi:10.3390/jof12040269
datoms.measure: Editing efficiency at ura3 locus (percentage of edited transformants)
datoms.methodology: Agrobacterium-mediated transformation with dual antibiotic selection
datoms.notes: Editing efficiency was relatively low at 14.9 percent, delivery used ATMT-based plasmids rather than RNP complexes, and off-target results are reported only as none detected at 8 tested sites rather than as a quantitative rate.

datoms.claim: LbCas12a ribonucleoprotein complexes achieve higher editing efficiency (32.3%) in rice PDS gene compared to WT Cas9 (3.6%) and HiFi Cas9 (8.8%).
datoms.source: R. Banakar, Mollie S. Schubert, Michael A. Collingwood, Christopher A. Vakulskas, A. Eggenberger. "Comparison of CRISPR-Cas9/Cas12a Ribonucleoprotein Complexes for Genome Editing Efficiency in the Rice Phytoene Desaturase (OsPDS) Gene" (2020). doi:10.1186/s12284-019-0365-z
datoms.population: Rice (Oryza sativa) embryos, 5-day-old mature seed derived
datoms.measure: Editing efficiency (percentage of edited lines detected by NGS)
datoms.methodology: Biolistic delivery of RNP complexes with NGS analysis
datoms.sample_size: 31 LbCas12a lines, 56 WT Cas9 lines, 34 HiFi Cas9 lines analyzed by NGS
datoms.notes: Sample size was small, only one crRNA was tested per nuclease (except Cas9 D10A), analysis used mosaic callus tissue rather than regenerated plants, and AsCas12a was run at 28C rather than the 37C typical for human cells, which may have reduced its apparent efficiency.

datoms.claim: CRISPR-Cas9 systems enable high efficiency genome editing across diverse organisms.
datoms.source: Saurabh Mishra, Samrah Rehan, Ahmad Mujtaba Barekzai, Ambika Sharma, Alok Raghav. "Emerging frontiers in genome editing: From CRISPR to next-generation technologies." (2026). doi:10.1016/j.ymeth.2026.05.011
datoms.measure: Editing efficiency
datoms.methodology: Literature review
datoms.notes: The paper acknowledges that off-target effects, immunogenicity, and germline ethics remain unresolved barriers to clinical translation.

datoms.claim: CRISPR/Cas9 enables efficient genome editing in cassava (Manihot esculenta), with editing efficiency reaching 90-100% in two cultivars.
datoms.source: John Odipio, Titus Alicai, Ivan Ingelbrecht, Dmitri A. Nusinow, Rebecca Bart. "Efficient CRISPR/Cas9 Genome Editing of Phytoene desaturase in Cassava" (2017). doi:10.3389/fpls.2017.01780
datoms.measure: Editing efficiency (percentage of plant lines with albino phenotype and confirmed mutations)
datoms.methodology: Agrobacterium-mediated transformation with molecular sequencing validation
datoms.sample_size: 38 plant lines sequenced (19 from each cultivar)
datoms.notes: T-DNA integration is not ideal for breeding improved germplasm given cassava's heterozygosity and inbreeding depression, and minor 1 bp off-target substitutions and deletions were observed near the target region.

datoms.claim: CRISPR-Cas9 system enables precise site-directed point mutations in bacterial genomes, with 95% efficiency for single nucleotide substitutions in Corynebacterium glutamicum.
datoms.source: Bo Wang, Qitiao Hu, Yu Zhang, Ruilin Shi, Xin Chai. "A RecET-assisted CRISPR–Cas9 genome editing in Corynebacterium glutamicum" (2018). doi:10.1186/s12934-018-0910-2
datoms.measure: Site-directed mutation efficiency (%)
datoms.methodology: Experimental site-directed mutagenesis with DNA sequencing verification
datoms.notes: Testing was limited to the pgi and argB genes, and the method requires careful repair-template design to avoid re-cleavage.

datoms.claim: Cas9 nuclease systems enable efficient genome editing in human cells, with editing efficiency measurable and reportable.
datoms.source: Mitchell O Roth, Yuerong Shu, Yu Zhao, Despoina Trasanidou, Renee D Hoffman. "Molecular basis for methylation-sensitive editing by Cas9." (2026). doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10384-z
datoms.population: Human cell lines with distinct DNA methylation landscapes
datoms.measure: Genome editing efficiency by ThermoCas9 in human cells
datoms.methodology: In vitro biochemistry and human cell genome editing
datoms.notes: The paper does not report quantitative off-target rates or compare efficiency across cell types or organisms beyond human cell lines.

datoms.claim: A designed SuperFi-Cas9 variant with mutations in the RuvC loop domain achieves 500-fold reduction in off-target (18–20 MM) cleavage while maintaining wild-type on-target cleavage rates (~2 s−1).
datoms.source: Jack P. K. Bravo, Mu-Sen Liu, Grace N. Hibshman, Tyler L. Dangerfield, Kyungseok Jung. "Structural basis for mismatch surveillance by CRISPR–Cas9" (2022). doi:10.1038/s41586-022-04470-1
datoms.population: Wild-type SpCas9 and engineered 7-D mutant (SuperFi-Cas9) with synthetic DNA substrates
datoms.measure: On-target and off-target DNA cleavage rates; specificity ratio in competition assay
datoms.methodology: Kinetic analysis and site-directed mutagenesis of Cas9 variants
datoms.sample_size: Multiple kinetic replicates and competition assays (not explicitly stated)
datoms.notes: The work was done in vitro with synthetic DNA substrates, so it may not fully predict in vivo performance, and further study is needed on the kinetic basis of the discrimination change.

datoms.claim: TALENs enable genome editing in plant organellar genomes (mitochondrial and plastid) with documented capability.
datoms.source: Chang Zhou, Shin-Ichi Arimura. "TALENs and Related Technologies for Editing Nuclear and Organellar Genomes in a Model Plant, Arabidopsis thaliana." (2026). doi:10.21769/BioProtoc.5668
datoms.domain: Plant biotechnology and organellar genome editing
datoms.measure: TALEN-mediated genome editing capability in plant organellar genomes
datoms.methodology: Protocol development and vector construction
datoms.notes: This protocol paper does not report quantitative editing efficiency or off-target rates for organellar genome editing.

datoms.claim: TnpB (a CRISPR-related nuclease) enables efficient genome editing in E. coli with documented editing efficiency rates.
datoms.source: Qian Guo, Qi Shen, Lixiang Zhao, Xiaoting Zhou, Sunjian Yan. "One Plasmid Is All You Need: Genome Editing in Escherichia coli Using Endogenous TnpB and Endogenous Recombination System." (2026). doi:10.1002/bit.70281
datoms.measure: Genome editing efficiency (percentage of cells with successful edits at target loci)
datoms.methodology: In vivo genome editing with plasmid-based system
datoms.notes: Testing was limited to a single bacterial strain (BL21 DE3), off-target rates were not explicitly reported, and broader applicability to other bacterial species is not yet demonstrated.

datoms.claim: CRISPR/Cas9 systems enable reproducible genome editing in fungal organisms without significant adverse effects on cellular phenotypes when Cas9 is stably expressed.
datoms.source: Jiawei Sun, Zichao Hu, Yingwu Yang. "An ATMT-CRISPR/Cas9 system for genome editing in Monascus purpureus." (2026). doi:10.1007/s11274-026-04943-9
datoms.population: Monascus purpureus with stably integrated Cas9 expression cassette
datoms.measure: Cellular phenotype assessment (growth, reproduction, pigment biosynthesis)
datoms.methodology: Agrobacterium tumefaciens-mediated transformation with stable Cas9 integration
datoms.notes: The study does not provide quantitative growth, reproduction, or pigment production comparisons between wild-type and Cas9-expressing strains.

datoms.claim: CRISPOR supports efficiency scoring for non-SpCas9 nucleases including SaCas9 and Cpf1, enabling genome editing efficiency prediction across multiple CRISPR nuclease systems.
datoms.source: J. Concordet, M. Haeussler. "CRISPOR: intuitive guide selection for CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing experiments and screens" (2018). doi:10.1093/nar/gky354
datoms.population: Guide RNA sequences for SaCas9, Cpf1, and SpCas9 across multiple genomes
datoms.measure: Efficiency prediction scores for non-SpCas9 CRISPR nucleases
datoms.methodology: Web tool implementation with integrated efficiency prediction algorithms for multiple nucleases
datoms.notes: The paper does not provide quantitative validation data for the SaCas9 and Cpf1 efficiency scores within CRISPOR itself.

datoms.claim: CRISPR/Cas9-based genome editing achieves efficient multiplex knockout in the fungal organism Acremonium chrysogenum, with documented editing efficiencies ranging from 50.0% to 95.5% depending on target number and promoter selection.
datoms.source: Zhen Chen, Wei Hong, Xiaorong Wei, Yifan Li, Tao Feng. "A Versatile tRNA-gRNA Array-Based CRISPR/Cas9 Platform Enabling Multiplex Genome Editing and Large-Fragment Engineering in Acremonium chrysogenum." (2026). doi:10.1021/acssynbio.6c00052
datoms.population: Acremonium chrysogenum wild-type and industrial strains
datoms.domain: Fungal genome engineering and metabolic engineering
datoms.measure: Knockout efficiency (percentage of successful edits at single, double, and triple loci)
datoms.methodology: Multiplex genome editing with tRNA-gRNA arrays in fungal strain
datoms.notes: The paper does not report off-target editing rates, nor detailed study duration or sample sizes for individual experiments.

datoms.claim: CRISPR-associated transposases (CASTs) enable RNA-guided DNA insertion across diverse bacterial species.
datoms.source: Thea C T Irvine, Andrew M Bailey, Thomas E Gorochowski. "A Golden Gate-Compatible CRISPR-Associated Transposon Tool for Multiplexed Bacterial Genome Editing." (2026). doi:10.1007/978-1-0716-5304-3_2
datoms.population: Diverse bacterial species including Escherichia coli BL21
datoms.domain: Synthetic biology and bacterial genome engineering
datoms.measure: Functional RNA-guided DNA insertion capability across bacterial species
datoms.methodology: Tool development and validation study
datoms.notes: The paper does not report quantitative editing efficiency or off-target rates for the CAST system.

datoms.claim: CRISPR/Cas9-based genome editing enables targeted editing of upstream open reading frames (uORFs) in fungal organisms.
datoms.source: Mengqian Liu, Sijin Chen, Jingting Wang, Guoliang Meng, Caihong Dong. "OmniEdit: A unified CRISPR/Cas9 platform for precise genome engineering and strain optimization of the Cordyceps militaris cell factory." (2026). doi:10.1016/j.synbio.2026.04.015
datoms.measure: Successful targeted uORF editing with introduction of premature stop codons
datoms.methodology: PEG-mediated protoplast transformation with CRISPR/Cas9 targeting uORF sequences
datoms.notes: The study does not report uORF editing efficiency as a percentage of transformants, and the functional impact on GABA production is not quantified.

datoms.claim: CRISPR-based nuclease systems exhibit off-target effects that represent a documented safety concern.
datoms.source: Saurabh Mishra, Samrah Rehan, Ahmad Mujtaba Barekzai, Ambika Sharma, Alok Raghav. "Emerging frontiers in genome editing: From CRISPR to next-generation technologies." (2026). doi:10.1016/j.ymeth.2026.05.011
datoms.measure: Off-target effects documentation
datoms.methodology: Literature review
datoms.notes: The paper treats off-target effects as a general unresolved challenge without organism-specific data or detailed characterization.

datoms.claim: Cas9/sgRNA-mediated genome editing achieves high editing efficiency in citrus, with mutation rates ranging from 21.43% to 100% at the target locus.
datoms.source: Hongge Jia, Zhuyuan Hu, Hao Wu, Yucheng Duan, Janice Zale. "Cas9/sgRNA-mediated genome editing of citrus via mature tissue transformation enables both high-efficacy genome editing and early flowering." (2026). doi:10.3389/fpls.2026.1852804
datoms.population: Valencia sweet orange (Citrus sinensis) mature internodal stem segments
datoms.measure: Cas9/sgRNA-mediated mutation frequency at target locus EBEpthA4-TI CsLOBP
datoms.methodology: Agrobacterium-mediated mature tissue transformation with Sanger sequencing
datoms.sample_size: 3 independent transgenic lines, 50 sequenced colonies per line
datoms.notes: Biallelic and homozygous mutations were achieved less successfully than with epicotyl or embryogenic protoplast methods, and the plants generated were transgenic; non-transgenic genome-edited citrus was not explored here.

datoms.claim: Transient expression of CRISPR/Cas9 RNA (in vitro transcripts) in wheat produces transgene-free mutants with 100% frequency in the T0 generation, with no detectable integration of external nucleic acids.
datoms.source: Yi Zhang, Zhen Liang, Yuan Zong, Yanpeng Wang, Jin‐Xing Liu. "Efficient and transgene-free genome editing in wheat through transient expression of CRISPR/Cas9 DNA or RNA" (2016). doi:10.1038/ncomms12617
datoms.population: Hexaploid bread wheat (Triticum aestivum L., cv. Kenong199)
datoms.domain: Plant genome editing; transgene-free genome editing
datoms.measure: Frequency of transgene-free mutants in T0 generation
datoms.methodology: Biolistic bombardment with in vitro transcribed Cas9 mRNA and sgRNA; PCR detection of transgenes
datoms.sample_size: 1,600 bombarded immature embryos; 17 T0 mutants identified
datoms.notes: The RNA-based TECCRNA method had a lower mutagenesis frequency (1.1 percent) than the DNA-based TECCDNA method (3.3 percent), possibly due to RNA instability and degradation, and RNA preparation is noted as more difficult to work with than DNA delivery.

datoms.claim: Off-target genome editing at predicted off-target sites is not detected in CRISPR/Cas9-edited Marchantia polymorpha lines with on-target mutations.
datoms.source: Shigeo S. Sugano, Ryuichi Nishihama, Makoto Shirakawa, Junpei Takagi, Y. Matsuda. "Efficient CRISPR/Cas9-based genome editing and its application to conditional genetic analysis in Marchantia polymorpha" (2018). doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0205117
datoms.population: Marchantia polymorpha T1 transformants with confirmed on-target mutations (39 plants for ARF1_1; 32 plants for NOP1_1)
datoms.measure: Off-target mutation rate at predicted off-target sites
datoms.methodology: Genomic DNA sequencing of predicted off-target sites
datoms.sample_size: 39 plants sequenced for ARF1_1 off-target sites; 32 plants sequenced for NOP1_1 off-target sites
datoms.notes: Only the three most likely off-target sites were analyzed, lower-probability sites were not assessed, and whether off-target mutations accumulate over prolonged culture or generations was not tested.

datoms.claim: TALENs enable site-specific DNA cleavage for genome editing applications.
datoms.source: Saurabh Mishra, Samrah Rehan, Ahmad Mujtaba Barekzai, Ambika Sharma, Alok Raghav. "Emerging frontiers in genome editing: From CRISPR to next-generation technologies." (2026). doi:10.1016/j.ymeth.2026.05.011
datoms.measure: Site-specific DNA cleavage capability
datoms.methodology: Literature review
datoms.notes: The paper does not provide quantitative efficiency or off-target data for TALENs, treating them only as a foundational method with inherent limitations.

datoms.claim: SpCas9-HF1 substantially reduces off-target mutations for sgRNAs targeting repetitive or homopolymeric sequences, with 123 of 144 off-target sites for a cytosine-rich homopolymeric target and 31 of 32 off-target sites for a TG-repeat target rendered undetectable.
datoms.source: Benjamin P. Kleinstiver, Vikram Pattanayak, Michelle S. Prew, Shengdar Q. Tsai, Nathalie T. Nguyen. "High-fidelity CRISPR–Cas9 nucleases with no detectable genome-wide off-target effects" (2016). doi:10.1038/nature16526
datoms.population: Human U2OS cells with sgRNAs targeting VEGFA homopolymeric and repetitive sequences
datoms.domain: Genome editing; CRISPR-Cas9 specificity on challenging sequences
datoms.measure: Off-target site reduction for repetitive and homopolymeric target sequences
datoms.methodology: GUIDE-seq in human cells with challenging repetitive target sequences
datoms.sample_size: 2 sgRNAs (VEGFA site 2 and VEGFA site 3); 144 and 32 potential off-target sites respectively
datoms.notes: Testing was limited to two challenging repetitive or homopolymeric sequences in the VEGFA gene, and only in human cells; the mechanism behind the specificity improvement needs further study.
